instructions.instruction: Use the HyperFrames skills. Start at /hyperframes (the router), then follow /general-video for the build — this is a custom 30-second, 5-scene composition, not a /faceless-explainer (that workflow targets 60–90s). Load /hyperframes-core before writing any HTML and /hyperframes-animation before writing the timeline. If a skill is missing, run `npx hyperframes skills update <name>`.

Work in /home/ow/projects/hyperframes-video. Each explainer is its own HyperFrames project at /home/ow/projects/hyperframes-video/videos/<slug>/ (slug = short lowercase topic, e.g. `pytorch`). Scaffold it from the videos/ folder with `npx --yes hyperframes@0.8.81 init <slug> --non-interactive --resolution=portrait --example=blank`. Do not modify the root index.html — that is a separate video.
Run all hyperframes commands from inside the video's project folder, using its npm scripts (they pin the CLI version).
Create an educational explainer video that teaches "$explainer_video_title".

safeZone.description: All text and key content must stay within the safe zone. Nothing important should touch the edges.

minimumFontSizes.note: Nothing under 28px — it's unreadable on mobile.

assets.note: Copy each asset into the video's project folder and reference it by relative path — compositions must not load files from outside the project.

asset.usage: Incorporate the headshot into the final scene CTA (circular crop, soft drop shadow, animated entrance).
Add as a background music track across the full composition. Trim to fit the 30-second duration.

mixing.rule: Fade in over the first 0.4s (12 frames): `data-fade-in="0.4"`.
Fade out over the last 0.6s (18 frames): `data-fade-out="0.6"`.
Keep volume low enough not to overpower any future voiceover: `data-volume` ~0.3–0.4.

step.name: Research & Script
step.description: Before writing any code, research the topic and write a 5-scene script.

sceneRequirements.requirement: Headline: "You can't afford to start? Check again." Explanation: You don't need money to start. You need to stop ignoring three assets you already own. Visual: A wallet icon in the center flips open and comes up empty, with "$0" stamped over it. Three locked boxes then slide in beside it in a row, numbered 1, 2 and 3.

Headline: "Your reputation" Explanation: People already trust you to deliver. That's what clients pay for, whether or not you have a website. Visual: Box 1 unlocks and opens into a résumé card. Endorsement chips ("Reliable", "Knows the field", "Gets it done") stack up beside it, and the card turns into a tag that reads "Paid advice."

Headline: "Your network" Explanation: Your first clients are already in your contacts, and one email to them costs nothing. Visual: Box 2 unlocks. A single node at the center sends lines out to a growing web of contact avatars, and three of them light up with the tag "First clients."

Headline: "Pattern recognition" Explanation: You've watched the same problem go wrong for decades, and people will pay to skip those mistakes. Visual: Box 3 unlocks. A path animates through a maze and takes a wrong turn several times, with a "×" marking each one. A second path then draws straight to the exit with the tag "Premium pricing."

Headline: "Startup cost: $0" Explanation: "The money was never the hard part. Using what you already have is." Visual: The three open boxes slide together into one stack, and a "$0" count-down lands under it. The circular headshot springs in over subtle rising particles.

step.gate: Show me the script and wait for approval before coding.

step.name: Design & Animate
step.description: After I approve the script, build all 5 scenes in the project's index.html (one `.clip` scene element per scene, or sub-compositions under compositions/ if a scene gets large) with the specs below.

visualStyle.assets: All icons/diagrams built as inline SVG (no external images except the headshot). No emoji — draw icons as SVG.

animationRules.rule: Everything is driven by the one paused GSAP root timeline registered on `window.__timelines` — no CSS animations or transitions that run on their own clock.
Every element enters with a smooth, no-overshoot ease (`power3.out` or `expo.out`) — no linear motion.
Diagrams and flowcharts should draw themselves (SVG `stroke-dashoffset` tweened on the timeline; use `pathLength="1"`).
Key numbers use a count-up: tween a plain object on the timeline and write the rounded value in `onUpdate`; style the number with `font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums`.
Final scene: particle effect background (10–15 circles drifting upward). Positions, sizes and speeds must be hard-coded or come from a seeded function — never `Math.random()`.
Loops (pulses, glows) use a finite `repeat`, never `repeat: -1`, so the timeline has a defined end and can be seeked.

sceneGuidance.principle: Each scene should have a clear visual metaphor — diagrams, flowcharts, icons, or step-by-step animations.
sceneGuidance.reference: Kurzgesagt meets Fireship: dense information, beautiful motion, fast pacing.

step.gate: Run `npm run check` and fix every error (review warnings) before moving on.

step.name: Final Scene CTA
step.description: The last scene must feature the headshot alongside the call to action.

requirements.requirement: Place the headshot in a circular frame, sized so the face stays well within the safe zone.
Animate the headshot in with a scale + fade.
Pair with a clear CTA headline (≥56px) and a short supporting line (≥36px).
Keep particle background subtle so the headshot and CTA remain the focal point.

step.name: Audio
step.description: Add the background music to the composition.

requirements.requirement: Use a single `<audio>` element at the root with `data-start="0"` and `data-duration="30"` so it plays across all scenes.
Apply the fades and volume from the backgroundMusic asset with `data-fade-in`, `data-fade-out` and `data-volume`.
The source file is longer than 30 seconds: let `data-duration` trim it (use `data-media-start` only to start later in the track) — never let it cut hard without the fade-out.

step.name: Preview
step.description: After building, launch HyperFrames Studio so I can preview the video in my browser. Use the agent-safe background preview, confirm it is listening, and give me the URL.
step.command: cd /home/ow/projects/hyperframes-video/videos/<slug> && npx --yes hyperframes@0.8.81 preview --background && npx --yes hyperframes@0.8.81 preview --status

step.name: Render
step.description: Render the final MP4 so it can be uploaded.

requirements.requirement: Use Node 20+ (run `nvm use 25` first if the system Node is older).
Output to `/home/ow/projects/hyperframes-video/out/`. Filename should match the slug (e.g. `pytorch.mp4`).
Background the render if it's long-running so other work can continue in parallel.
Verify the result with ffprobe: 1080×1920, h264 video, AAC audio, ~30s.

step.name: Schedule
step.description: Schedule the rendered video to X, YouTube, Threads, Instagram, and TikTok in the next empty slot using the Blotato MCP.

accounts.note: Use the AI/tech explainer series account IDs in /home/ow/.claude/projects/-home-ow-projects-claude-remotion/memory/content-brand-accounts.md. Do not ask which account to use — that table is the source of truth.

workflow.step: 1. Call `blotato_create_presigned_upload_url` with the local filename to get back `presignedUrl` + `publicUrl`.
2. PUT the raw MP4 bytes to `presignedUrl` with `Content-Type: video/mp4` (no JSON, no multipart). Confirm HTTP 200.

3. Find the next empty slot: call `blotato_list_schedules` (paginate with `cursor` until no cursor is returned — other sessions fill this queue too). Slots are 14:00, 18:00 and 22:00 UTC daily. Pick the earliest future slot with no posts on any of the 5 accounts.
4. For each of the 5 platforms, call `blotato_create_post` with an explicit `scheduledTime` set to that slot (ISO 8601 UTC), passing `publicUrl` in `mediaUrls`. Fire the 5 calls in parallel.

schedulingRules.rule: Do NOT use `useNextFreeSlot: true` — it does not skip slots that already have posts, so videos collide at the same minute.
Report times to the user in US Eastern (America/New_York); Blotato stores UTC.

captionRules.rule: Write one short hook caption ("What is X? <one-line value>. 30s ↓"). Re-use across platforms with minor per-platform tweaks.
Instagram: cap hashtags at 5 maximum. Required fields: `mediaType: "reel"`, `shareToFeed: true`.
YouTube: required fields: `title`, `privacyStatus: "public"`, `shouldNotifySubscribers: true`. Body text becomes the description — include hashtags there.

TikTok: required fields — `privacyLevel: "PUBLIC_TO_EVERYONE"`, `disabledComments: false`, `disabledDuet: false`, `disabledStitch: false`, `isBrandedContent: false`, `isYourBrand: false`, `isAiGenerated: true`. Also pass `title`.
X (twitter) and Threads: text-only caption — no extra required fields.

step.gate: After all 5 posts are queued, report the 5 `postSubmissionId`s so I can verify in the Blotato dashboard.
